headline: Growth holds steady, profit spike is a one-time tax gain
summary_short: Revenue for the quarter ended April 30, 2026 was $450.7M, up 8.5% y/y but roughly flat q/q (+0.2%); net income of $435.9M was driven almost entirely by a one-time ~$434.9M release of deferred-tax valuation allowances, not operating performance, which stayed a loss.
summary_long: Q4 FY2026 (three months ended April 30, 2026) revenue was $450.7M, +8.5% y/y and roughly flat q/q; full FY2026 revenue rose 17% to $1.739B, led by Elastic Cloud (+22% FY) and Annual Elastic Cloud (+28% FY). FY subscription gross margin rose to 81% from 80% on cloud-hosting efficiencies, but rising opex (FY R&D +24%, S&M +15%, G&A +11%, mostly personnel and stock comp) pushed quarterly operating income to -$16.4M. Net income of $435.9M was driven almost entirely by a ~$434.9M release of deferred-tax valuation allowances (Netherlands, UK, California). FY2026 operating cash flow was $326.9M; Elastic repurchased $340.0M of stock under its $500M buyback authorization. No forward guidance was issued in this 10-K.

drivers.explanation: FY2026 subscription revenue grew 18% (services +6%), driven by Elastic Cloud adoption (+22% FY) with Annual Elastic Cloud up 28% FY, per the release — a full-year figure, not isolated to this quarter.

FY subscription gross margin improved to 81% from 80% on cloud-hosting cost efficiencies, per the release, but the quarter's own gross margin (75.4%) was down q/q and y/y; the filing gives no Q4-only cause.

FY R&D (+24%), sales & marketing (+15%), and G&A (+11%) expense growth — mostly higher personnel costs, stock-based comp, and commissions per the release — outpaced revenue growth, pushing quarterly operating income negative.
Not a line item in the filing (which reports operating loss and pre-tax loss); EBIT's swing to negative tracks the same opex growth described for operating income.
Not a company-reported figure; EBITDA's decline tracks the operating-income decline, since FY depreciation and intangible amortization ($11.8M) is modest relative to the swing.

Net income of $435.9M this quarter came almost entirely from a ~$434.9M release of deferred-tax valuation allowances in the Netherlands ($390.5M), UK ($23.7M), and California ($20.7M), per the release — not from operating results, which stayed a loss.
Tracks net income's tax-driven jump; share count was not materially changed by the quarter's buyback activity relative to the size of the tax benefit.
Same one-time deferred-tax valuation-allowance release described for net income and basic EPS; not an operating-performance improvement.
Net Expansion Rate was approximately 112% as of April 30, 2026, per the release, indicating continued expansion within the existing customer base alongside the swing in reported profitability.
